title: Receivables Advance Rate on Operating Lines of Credit and the Certificate Reporting Record
content:
The advance rate on eligible receivables reported on an Operating Lines of Credit borrowing base certificate turns on how many certificates the line has on record with an as-of date within the twelve whole months before today.

## Rule

Receivables are lent against at:

- **60 percent** when fewer than 6 certificates on the line have an as-of date within the twelve whole months before today;
- **70 percent** when at least 6 but fewer than 11 do;
- **the product's advance rate on receivables** when 11 or more do.

The certificate being figured counts among them.

## Rates by product (percent of face value)

| Product | Fewer than 6 certificates | 6 to 10 certificates | 11 or more certificates (product rate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Borrowing Base Operating Line | 60 | 70 | 80 |
| Agribusiness Revolving Line | 60 | 70 | 85 |
| StartRight Operating Line, ExpressLine Operating Credit, Seasonal Operating Loan, Revolving Operating Line | 60 | 70 | 0 |

## Counting table (hypothetical Borrowing Base Operating Line)

| Certificates with an as-of date in the twelve whole months before today, the one being figured included | Rate on receivables |
|---|---|
| 5 | 60% |
| 6 | 70% |
| 10 | 70% |
| 11 | 80% |

## Question on the rule

**A member delivers a first certificate after a long gap. Does it count toward the total?** Yes. The certificate being figured is one of the certificates counted, provided its as-of date falls within the twelve whole months before today.
